subject: PrivDeploy: cost redistribution & exit funding request
messages:
From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@peregrinehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jill Park <jill.park@peregrinehealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-14 09:12 -0700
Subject: Platform fee treatment + exit funding (RFP follow-up)

Marissa — thanks for the demo last week. Peregrine's procurement and finance teams have one outstanding concern before we move this to legal: the platform fee for Private (VPC/on-prem) looks large relative to our usage pattern, and our CFO is worried about the sunk cost if we ever replatform. Two asks: 1) Can you show a clear amortization or redistribution approach for the platform fee so it behaves more like capex over time? 2) Are you willing to provide an explicit migration/exit funding mechanism (a refundable or transferable credit) if we move off Redwood within a defined window?

We also need an SRE/ops retainer breakdown — our SREs expect a predictable on-call SLA with a defined price. If you can provide a worked example (numbers) for a 3-year commit and an 18-month exit scenario, that will speed sign-off.

Happy to hop on a call but wanted to get examples in writing first.

Carlos
VP, IT Procurement
Peregrine Health

Attachments: Peregrine_RFP_attachments.zip (referenced)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@peregrinehealth.com>
Cc: Jill Park <jill.park@peregrinehealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-14 12:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Platform fee treatment + exit funding (RFP follow-up)

Carlos — appreciate the clear ask. I've pulled finance and offerings together and attached a workbook that shows three approaches plus example math for a 3-year commit with an 18-month exit. High level options we can propose: 

- Option A (Amortized Platform Fee): Platform fee invoiced up-front but amortized for accounting purposes; if Peregrine exits early, remaining amortized value converts to a service credit applied against final invoices (no cash refund).
- Option B (Implementation Credit + Migration Fund): Offer a one-time implementation credit (applied against year 1 platform fee) and seed a migration fund (cash-hold/credit) that reduces net cost of migration.
- Option C (Tiered Exit Protection): For multi-year committed customers, provide a refundable migration credit that scales with the commit level and time-in-contract (e.g., 50% of remaining pro-rata platform fee refundable if exit in year 1, 25% in year 2; subject to cap).

SRE/ops retainer tiers (examples):
- Bronze: 8x5 email support, 8h response SLA, $6k/mo
- Silver: 24x7 paging for sev1, 2h response SLA, $18k/mo + 40h/month runbook work
- Gold: 24x7 paging + on-site quarterly engineering reviews, 30m sev1 SLA, $35k/mo + priority engineering

I've attached the workbook (redwood_platform_fee_workbook.xlsx) that has the numeric scenarios. If you prefer, we can translate Option B into a refundable mechanism instead of credits — finance will need to sign off.

Next step — pick one approach and we'll produce a redlineable term sheet + SOW. Would you have 30 minutes tomorrow to walk through the numbers?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_platform_fee_workbook.xlsx (contains amortization tables and proposed caps)

From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@peregrinehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15 08:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Platform fee treatment + exit funding (RFP follow-up)

Marissa — thanks, received the workbook and it helps. Two clarifying questions after a quick pass: 

1) For Option C (Tiered Exit Protection) can you show a worked numeric example: our proposed deal is a 3-year commit with a $1.2M platform fee paid in year 1; if we move after 18 months, how much cash or credit would we actually see under your language?
2) Can you cap the maximum refundable amount (we'd prefer no open-ended liability on Redwood's side) — if so, what's Redwood comfortable with by tier?

Also, our legal wants a specific clause we can show to the board: some language about an "Exit Fund" or "Migration Credit" and how it's triggered. Can you share a draft term sheet/phrase we can circulate while legal does a first pass?

If you can send a short illustrative term-sheet paragraph and the sample math, we can feed to legal. Otherwise happy to do a call today after 3pm PT.

Carlos

On Thu, Jul 14, 2026 at 12:05 PM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> (attached workbook)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15 10:15 -0700
Subject: RE: Platform fee treatment + exit funding (RFP follow-up)

Marissa — jumped in with the numbers Carlos asked for. Quick model notes (see attached term_sheet_redwood_peregrine_20260714.docx):

- Numeric example (Option C, Tiered Exit Protection):
  * Total platform fee: $1,200,000 (paid Y1)
  * Time of exit: 18 months (1.5 years) => remaining pro-rata platform fee = $1,200,000 * (3 - 1.5) / 3 = $600,000
  * Refundable percentage (per tier): 50% refundable in year 1 exits; 25% refundable in year 2. For this example: 50% * $600,000 = $300,000 credit/refund cap.
  * Maximum payable cap suggestion: $250,000 for Starter, $500,000 for Committed, $1,000,000 for Enterprise (limits to protect Redwood).

- Alternative (lower liability): Convert refund to a migration credit applied over 12 months of post-exit invoices (better cash-flow control).

- Escrow/trigger: propose an agreed-upon trigger event (customer issues migration notice with 90 days' written notice + evidence of executed hosting agreement) and funds are payable after independent audit confirms migrated state.

- SRE retainer: recommended pricing lines match Marissa's examples; finance prefers retainer rather than hourly runbook credits.

If we offer the cap structure above and a migration-credit fallback, I think we can balance Peregrine's ask and Redwood's liability. I drafted term-sheet language and attached. Happy to tweak.

Karthik
VP, Head of Commercial Finance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: term_sheet_redwood_peregrine_20260714.docx (draft paragraph + caps table)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@peregrinehealth.com>
Cc: Jill Park <jill.park@peregrinehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15 15:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Platform fee treatment + exit funding (RFP follow-up)

Carlos — thanks for the patience. Consolidating our proposal below (attached: Draft_SOW_Peregrine_v2.pdf and term sheet):

Proposal summary (pick one):
- Starter (low commit): amortized platform fee + migration credit fallback
  * Platform fee: $1,200,000
  * Exit protection: migration credit equal to 50% of remaining pro-rata platform fee, capped at $250k
  * SRE retainer: Bronze ($6k/mo)

- Committed (recommended for Peregrine): 3-year commit, implementation credit $150k, refundable migration fund
  * Platform fee: $1,200,000 less $150k implementation credit applied in Y1
  * Exit protection: refundable credit = 50% of remaining pro-rata, capped at $500k, or migration credit applied over 12 months (customer choice)
  * SRE retainer: Silver ($18k/mo) included for first 6 months
- Enterprise: 3-year commit + higher entitlements
  * Platform fee: negotiated
  * Exit protection: refundable credit up to $1M; shorter refund window (year 1 only)
  * SRE retainer: Gold ($35k/mo) + quarterly onsite

Next steps: 1) Which option best maps to Peregrine's risk profile? 2) If Committed, we'll send a redlineable term sheet and draft SOW for legal review today. 3) Proposed call: Fri 7/16, 10:00am PT to finalize.

If that timing works, I'll book the call and loop in legal.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Draft_SOW_Peregrine_v2.pdf, term_sheet_redwood_peregrine_20260714.docx
